newsitem.title: USA: Dollar falls after Bundesbank chief says rally at an end.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls after Bundesbank chief says rally at an end.

text.p: The dollar fell from a 3-1/2-year high against the mark on Thursday after Germany's top central banker said he believed the dollar has made a full recovery from its all-time lows in 1995.
The yen weakened against the mark as well, which indirectly helped bolster the dollar against the Japanese currency.

Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, speaking after the central bank's biweekly policy-setting meeting, also said it was important for the mark to remain strong until the introduction of the new single European currency, the euro.
"There was definitely a very strong correlation with Tietmeyer and (the dollar) coming down off the 1.7665 mark high overnight," said Bob Near, vice president at The Bank of New York.
The dollar fell nearly two pfennigs after extending this week's string of powerful gains in Tokyo trading to another peak not seen since February 1994.
The dollar fell to 1.7510 marks from 1.7605 marks late Wednesday, but rose to 113.11 Japanese yen from 112.75 yen.
The dollar hit a record low at 1.3438 marks in March 1995 and has strengthened around 31 percent since then.

This year alone, the dollar has appreciated almost 15 percent against the German currency, mostly on fears that the mark, the dominant currency for business and investment in Europe, would be supplanted with a weak euro.
The dollar was pressured after the British and Dutch central banks increased their official interest rates.
Higher interest rates in Europe diminish the appeal of dollar-denominated investments and it usually is easier to exchange dollars for marks than for less-traded currencies, like guilders.

The British pound fell against mark, indirectly dragging down the dollar, as dealers were disappointed that the Bank of England raised its base interest rate less than expected, by 1/4 of a percentage point to 6.75 percent.
The Netherlands raised a key money market rate to 3.0 percent from 2.9 percent.
In other trading, the pound firmed slightly to $1.6885 from $1.6875.
The dollar fell to 1.4485 Swiss francs from 1.4580 Swiss on Wednesday. It was unchanged at Canadian $1.3737.
